textbookText: Essentially, the high specific heat capacity of water allows it to act as a long-lasting heat reservoir, warming the body steadily and efficiently. (ii) 200 g of water at 30°C in a tray gets changed into water at 0°C when it is placed inside the deep freezer of a refrigerator for sometimes. Calculate the heat released by the water in this process. (Ans: 25.2 KJ) Ans:- Given, mass of the water (m) = 200g = 0.2kg Change in temperature (dt) = 30°C - 0°C = 30°C Specific heat capacity (s) = 4200 J/kg°C Heat released (Q) = ? We know that, Q = msdt = 0.2 * 30 * 4200 = 25200J = 25.2 KJ 9. Describe the working mechanism of digital thermometer and radiation thermometer. Ans:- Digital Thermometer: A digital thermometer works by using a sensor, usually a thermistor or a thermocouple, that changes its electrical resistance or voltage with temperature. When placed in contact with the body or object, the sensor detects the temperature and converts it into an electrical signal. This signal is processed by a microprocessor, which calculates the temperature and displays it digitally on a screen, providing a fast and accurate reading without the need for mercury or alcohol. Radiation Thermometer: A radiation thermometer measures temperature without direct contact by detecting the infrared radiation emitted by an object. The device contains a lens that focuses the infrared energy onto a detector, which converts it into an electrical signal proportional to the intensity of radiation. This signal is then processed to calculate the temperature of the object and displayed digitally, making it ideal for measuring hot, moving, or hard-to-reach surfaces safely. 10. Study the relationship between the volume and temperature of water shown in the given graph and answer the following questions i) What is the special property of water shown in the graph called? Define the property. Ans:- The special property shown is the Anomalous Expansion of Water. This is the unique behavior where water, unlike most liquids, contracts (volume decreases) when heated from 0°C to 4°C. At 4°C, it reaches its minimum volume, after which it begins to expand normally with increasing temperature. ii) Mention the change in volume of water that appears when water is heated from 0°C to 10 °C. Ans:- When heated from 0°C to 10°C, the volume change occurs in two distinct phases: from 0°C to 4°C, the water contracts and its volume decreases. From 4°C to 10°C, the water expands and its volume increases, behaving like most other liquids. iii) How does the property of water shown in the graph differ from the property of other liquids? Ans:- Water differs from most other liquids because it exhibits an initial phase of contraction when heated near its freezing point (0°C to 4°C). Other common liquids show a continuous expansion (volume increase) immediately upon being heated from their freezing point upwards, never contracting in this manner. 11. Study the relationship between the density and temperature of water shown in the given graph and answer the following questions. i) At what temperature density of water is maximum? Why? Ans:- The density of water is 4°C. This is because density is inversely proportional to volume (p = m/V), and due to the anomalous expansion property, water has its minimum volume precisely at this temperature, making its density the highest. ii) Write the importance of this knowledge in daily life Ans:- This knowledge is vital for the survival of aquatic life in cold regions. The densest water (4°C) sinks to the bottom of lakes and ponds, while colder, less dense water remains near the surface and freezes. The resulting layer of ice floats and acts as an insulator, keeping the water below at a warmer 4°C where fish and other organisms can survive. iii) Draw a model graph to show the relationship between the density of water and temperature based on the relationship shown in the graph. Ans:- A model graph for the density of water versus temperature shows a curve that rises sharply from 0°C to its peak at 4°C (maximum density), and then gradually falls as the temperature increases further. This shape is characteristic of water's anomalous behavior.
